preamble: Excrescence of [p] inserts a voiceless labial stop between the labial nasal [m] and a following voiceless obstruent (typically [s], [t] or [θ]). The stop arises when the velum rises before the lips open, producing an oral release with the place of [m] and the voicelessness of the next consonant.

examples.note: 'Vacant'. The p is a Middle English insertion between m and t.
Common variable pronunciation in RP and General American.
Variable pronunciation, often reflected in the spelling 'hampster'.
'Bought', perfect passive participle of emō 'buy'; p inserted in the m.t cluster.
'I took', perfect of sūmō; p inserted in the m.s cluster. Oniga and Re identify this as the only productive epenthesis in Classical Latin.

sources: Oniga, R. & Re, A. (2023). Consonant epenthesis in Latin. Journal of Latin Linguistics. https://doi.org/10.1515/joll-2022-2015
